findings.reason: a worker that regenerates those figures through the shared function measures up to 2.24e-3 against a stated 1e-3 and has no authority to widen the tolerance, so the gate fails on the shared function's declared-size precision or the criterion is quietly loosened; the plan has to say which quantity carries the ratio (and that the shared function must preserve it) or state a tolerance the declared-size precision can meet.
findings.text: §2's new invariant ("each figure file's exported width-to-height ratio equals its drawn canvas ratio within one part in a thousand") is unreachable for three tracked vector figures the section requires to be regenerated through the shared function, because that function declares the SVG height rounded to three significant digits (`imas_codex/plotting/style.py:75`, `height:.3g`): measured at the repository's HEAD, a 14x5.3in canvas (`docs/figures/discovery-to-mapping/mapping-lifecycle.svg`, drawn ratio 2.641509) exports as `31.1cm x 11.8cm`, ratio 2.635593, relative error 2.24e-3; a 14x10.32in canvas (`pickup-probe.svg`) gives 1.10e-3; and a 14x6.4in canvas (`docs/figures/ai-stack/ai-stack.svg`, drawn ratio 2.1875) gives 1.21e-3 against today's 14.22cm, which the script itself derives at two decimals — so the change replaces an invariant the current files meet with one the migration breaks, and the tolerance is exceeded for a reason unrelated to the migration itself

response_events.note: Section 2's done-when at version 9 takes the ratio from a vector file's coordinate box or a raster's pixel size, and requires the declared physical size to carry the same ratio within one part in a thousand, so the shared function must declare it precisely enough.
